newsitem.title: INDIA: Indian call money seen trading in narrow range.
newsitem.headline: Indian call money seen trading in narrow range.

text.p: Call money was traded in the 10.50-10.75 percent range on Thursday morning, slightly up from Wednesday's closing rate of 10.25-10.75 percent, dealers said.
Call money was expected to trade in a range between 10.50 and 10.75 percent on Thursday, they said.
"Even though rates have moved up from single-digit levels last week, liquidity remains reasonably good," a dealer at a state-run bank said. "Eleven percent remains a major barrier."
Dealers said there would be resistance at the 11 percent mark, the rate at which banks can avail refinance from the Reserve Bank of India against export credit.
"Banks have not yet drawn export refinance," a dealer said. "So some cushion remains in case liquidity dries up."
